overview: Black plays a Kan-style ...a6 before taking on d4, so White can avoid the open Sicilian with 4.c4 (a Maroczy-type bind) or 4.Bd3, or transpose with 4.dxc5. If White takes on c5 or plays 4.c4, Black has ...Nf6 and ...Nc6 or ...d6 and a Hedgehog-like set-up. I am unsure of the name and judge it from the moves.

white_ideas.idea: 4.c4 to clamp d5 with a Maroczy bind, then Nc3 and Be2
Or 4.dxc5 / 4.Bd3 to steer into a quieter game than the open Sicilian

black_ideas.idea: Hold ...a6 flexibility, ...Nf6, ...Nc6, ...d6, and break with ...d5 or ...b5
Transpose to Kan or Taimanov structures after 4.Nc3 cxd4

typical_structures.structure: Maroczy-type bind after c4, or a Kan/Taimanov Sicilian with ...e6/...d6

character.notes: Flexible, move-order Sicilian; positions range from quiet bind to normal Kan play.

soundness.notes: Sound; just a Kan move order that allows 4.c4.

structure.notes: Fixed asymmetric centre with a half-open c-file for Black.

approach.notes: A move-order twist within the Sicilian, played now and then.

level.notes: Black needs to know the Kan and Taimanov ideas but the plans are clear.

sublines_that_differ.name: Open Sicilian transposition
sublines_that_differ.how: Goes into the Kan with the usual sharp theory

character.reason: Flexible Kan-style Sicilian, neither especially solid nor forcing.

soundness.reason: A Kan move order, fully playable.

structure.reason: Sicilian asymmetric centre with a half-open file.

approach.reason: A recognised Sicilian move order, not a rarity strong players avoid.

level.reason: Needs the Kan and Maroczy ideas but not long forcing lines.
